core_obligations: Dispose of one implication and set up the local computation: purity relative to the base implies (by the universal purity lemma) that purity survives base change, and by fpqc descent of local projectivity it suffices to prove that the pushforward of the module is fpqc locally projective on the base; fix a point s and aim to show local projectivity on an etale neighbourhood (proof lines 5597-5607).

Produce the neighbourhood and remove the relative associated points: use the flat along the fibre lemma to get an affine diagram of finite presentation over an affine elementary etale neighbourhood, with g etale, the fibre at s inside g(X') and the global sections of the pulled back module projective over the ring of the base; since the pulled back module is universally pure, the purity criterion places the relative associated points over the localisation at s inside the open g(X'), the set of points of the base where the associated points of the fibre lie in g(X') is constructible and contains that localisation, hence contains an open neighbourhood of s, and after shrinking one may assume all relative associated points lie in g(X') (proof lines 5609-5639).

Conclude projectivity: that inclusion means the restriction map of global sections is universally injective over the ring of the base by the universal injectivity criterion, so the module of global sections is Mittag-Leffler; as it is also countably generated and flat over that ring, it is projective, which gives the required local projectivity of the pushforward (proof lines 5641-5653).
proof_roadmap: Use universal purity and fpqc descent of local projectivity to reduce to an etale local statement (proof lines 5597-5607).
Build the affine etale neighbourhood and, using purity, shrink the base so that the relative associated points lie in the image of the etale morphism (proof lines 5609-5639).
Convert that inclusion into Mittag-Leffler and then projectivity of the pushforward (proof lines 5641-5653).
difficulty_reason: The proposition characterises purity relative to the base, for an affine finitely presented morphism and a finitely presented flat module, as local projectivity of the pushforward, with the ring theoretic corollary that a flat finitely presented module over a finitely presented algebra is projective exactly when the associated sheaf is pure relative to the base (statement lines 5581-5595, tag 05MD). The proof is a real etale local computation: it reduces by fpqc descent to an etale neighbourhood, builds the affine etale neighbourhood with projective global sections, uses the purity criterion and constructibility to shrink the base until the relative associated points lie inside the image of the etale morphism, converts that inclusion into universal injectivity and then into the Mittag-Leffler property, and finally applies the countably generated flat projectivity criterion. The constructibility shrinking step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
